businessModel: Free; runs on your existing Claude Code or Codex plan
summary: Native Mac WebKit browser built around coding agents: press ⌘E on any page to turn it into a task for Claude Code or Codex, track parallel agent projects, and organize tabs by theme. Free, no new subscription.
bestFor: Developers who already pay for Claude Code or Codex
Mac users wanting agents as first-class citizens
People who prefer WebKit and Keychain
notFor: People who want a stand-alone cloud agent

pros.title: Agents beside the page
pros.detail: ⌘E sends page context to Claude Code or Codex while you keep browsing.

pros.title: No new subscription
pros.detail: Uses your existing Claude Code or Codex plan; no API keys.

pros.title: Keychain passwords
pros.detail: Saves to the Mac Keychain; 1Password works via universal autofill.

cons.title: No Chrome extensions yet
cons.detail: Maker plans "make your own extension" and is exploring support.

cons.title: Mac only, WebKit
cons.detail: Chrome-only sites and APIs may behave differently.

cons.title: Needs separate agent plan
cons.detail: Useless without Claude Code or Codex.

cons.title: Little documentation
cons.detail: License, privacy policy and version not stated.

faq.q: How does Rill differ from Atlas or Comet?
faq.a: It delegates to the coding agent you already use rather than shipping its own cloud agent.
Not yet; the maker is looking into it.
Yes, and it uses your Claude Code or Codex plan.
